slides.title: Alibaba Unveils Qwen-Robot Series for Embodied AI
slides.highlight: Alibaba has introduced the Qwen-Robot series of foundation models for embodied AI, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Alibaba Unveils Qwen Robot Suite for Embodied AI
slides.highlight: The introduction of the Qwen Robot Suite for embodied AI is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated learning.

slides.title: Evaluating Large Language Models Abilities for Addressee, Turn-change, and Next Speaker Prediction in Meetings
slides.highlight: This research evaluates LLMs and multimodal LLMs on addressee detection and speaker prediction, contributing to HyECHO's goals regarding addressee/listener modeling and team state perception.

card.one_liner: LLMs outperform humans and supervised models in next speaker prediction for multi-party meetings using conversational context.
card.key_idea: A unified framework evaluating addressee detection, turn-change, and next speaker prediction across supervised models, text-based LLMs, and multimodal LLMs (MM-LLMs).
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the AMI Meeting Corpus using accuracy and F1 scores, comparing models against supervised baselines and human subjects.
card.limitation: MM-LLMs struggle to effectively leverage raw audio-visual signals, and human evaluation was conducted by non-native English speakers.

slides.title: WaveSync: Constrained Wavefront Optimization for Synchronized Co-Speech Gestures in Humanoid Robots
slides.tldr: SYNCHRONIZED CO-SPEECH GESTURES FOR HUMANOID ROBOTS
slides.highlight: WaveSync uses a hybrid framework and wavefront optimization to align expressive gestures with speech while ensuring kinematic feasibility. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: WaveSync synchronizes humanoid robot gestures with speech emphasis while respecting strict physical kinematic constraints.
card.key_idea: An LLM generates a Semantic Importance Wave; Dynamic Movement Primitives shape trajectories, and a wavefront optimizer aligns gesture peaks to speech peaks using duration compression and forward propagation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via PyBullet simulations across five scenarios using objective metrics (HbS, Jerk) and subjective Likert ratings from 20 participants; outperformed three ablated baselines.
card.limitation: Relies on a fixed action library, limiting its ability to handle unconstrained dialogue; not yet tested on physical hardware.

slides.title: MuVAP: Multimodal Multiparty Voice Activity Projection for Turn-taking Prediction in the Wild
slides.highlight: MuVAP enables speaker-aware turn-taking predictions using monaural audio and a single camera, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling in hybrid teams.

card.one_liner: MuVAP predicts multiparty turn-taking using a single camera and monaural audio stream via multimodal projection.
card.key_idea: Uses Role-Relative Projection to map N-speaker dynamics onto a fixed current/next floor-holder state, grounding acoustic predictions in visual face tracks for speaker-aware forecasting.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the new 31-hour AVCC dataset using Shift-Hold and Next-Speaker Prediction tasks; outperformed MLP and unimodal baselines across 2- and 3-speaker settings.
card.limitation: Performance is lower in active prediction tasks compared to silent ones and decreases as the number of speakers increases.

slides.title: Adaptive Turn-Taking for Real-time Multi-Party Voice Agents
slides.highlight: This work introduces ModeratorLM, which uses role-playing and reasoning to improve turn-taking precision and reduce interruptions in multi-party conversations, supporting HyECHO's focus on listener modeling and engagement.

card.one_liner: ModeratorLM is a role-playing voice agent that adapts turn-taking behavior based on an assigned persona.
card.key_idea: A speech LLM processing streaming audio chunks, using role-conditioned fine-tuning and an optional chain-of-thought reasoning variant (ModeratorLM-Think) to decide when to intervene in multi-party conversations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on real-world meeting data (NSF-1) and synthetic RolePlayConv dataset; showed >40% precision and >70% recall improvements over non-role-conditioned baselines.
card.limitation: The model relies heavily on textual transcriptions for turn-taking decisions, with performance degrading substantially without them.

slides.title: Beyond Usability: A UX Case Study on Using "Withdrawal Design" to Challenge Engagement Metrics in Social Robotics
slides.tldr: CHALLENGING ENGAGEMENT METRICS IN SOCIAL ROBOTICS
slides.highlight: This study examines how the removal of a social robot can prompt children with autism to seek human interaction, suggesting that long-term engagement may sometimes silo social behavior. It is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: Withdrawal of social robots may better promote human social motivation than continued robot engagement.
card.key_idea: A mixed-methods "withdrawal design" comparing children who kept a social robot versus those who had it removed to evaluate long-term social bridging.
card.evaluation: 8-week home RCT (N=40) using SCARED, RCADS, SMS, RMET, and SUS metrics; results show a trade-off between anxiety reduction and social motivation.

slides.title: Fast When, Careful Who: Dual-Process Multiparty Turn-Taking with Diffusion Augmentation
slides.highlight: This work proposes a two-stage audio-only pipeline for multiparty turn-taking that separates turn boundary triggering from floor transfer verification, supporting HyECHO's focus on diarization and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: A dual-process audio pipeline for multiparty turn-taking using diffusion-based background augmentation to improve shift detection.
card.key_idea: A fast WavLM-based gate proposes turn boundaries, while a slow ECAPA-TDNN verifier confirms floor transfers (HOLD vs SHIFT) and predicts the next speaker.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on VoxConverse using precision, recall, F1, and MAE; compared against a ResCNN-Siamese baseline and VAP in dyadic settings.
card.limitation: Performance is constrained by boundary coverage, particularly in heavily overlapped or fast-exchange areas where acoustic cues are ambiguous.

slides.title: Co-Creating Buildable and Open Social Robot Study Companions with University Students
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates how Design for Assembly and Disassembly can lower barriers for students building social robots, supporting RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: DfA and DfD mechanical redesigns significantly improve the usability and perceived buildability of open-source social robots.
card.key_idea: Applied the Double Diamond framework to redesign the Robot Study Companion (v4.1) using twist-lock fasteners, snap-fit joints, and tool-free latches to reduce assembly friction and workload.
card.evaluation: Two studies with developers and first-time builders using SUS, NASA-TLX, and assembly timing; SUS improved from 59.4 to 89.4 for developers.
card.limitation: Small, non-random samples; potential self-evaluation bias from developers; lack of inter-rater reliability checks for thematic coding.
